value.body:
With `scheduler.tests` on, `cargo nextest run` now runs each test under the machine-wide scheduler, and nextest's `-j` no longer caps the build. This release also fixes several causes of cache misses and bypasses: explicit linkers, `-L native` directories, and build scripts that declare `OUT_DIR`. Workspace `staticlib`/`cdylib` libraries now compile incrementally, and `HOST_CC` no longer changes between a symlinked `mbx` and its real path.

## Added

- **`cargo nextest run` tests are scheduled in the shared pool** ([#684](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/684), @jbellis). Before, only compilers and `cargo test` binaries waited for permits. So several agents on one machine could each start a full nextest run at once and run out of memory. With `scheduler.tests = true` (or `MBX_SCHEDULER_TESTS=1`), each nextest test process now waits for permits from the same machine-wide pool as compilers:

  ```sh
  MBX_SCHEDULER_TESTS=1 mbx nextest run --workspace
  # or, for every run:
  mbx settings set scheduler.tests true
  ```

  - mbx installs its runner through `CARGO_TARGET_<TRIPLE>_RUNNER`. Any runner you configured is still called. Cargo aliases such as `[alias] nt = "nextest run"` are scheduled too.
  - mbx records each test's CPU and peak memory under `<cache>/scheduler/tests/` and uses them to size its permit request. A test with no history asks for 1 core and 2 permits of memory. `mbx gc` removes history that hasn't been used for 30 days.
  - Listing tests never waits.
  - **Timeouts:** nextest starts a test's `slow-timeout` clock, including `terminate-after`, when it starts the runner, so time spent waiting for a permit counts as test time. After a one-second wait, mbx writes a note to the test's stderr. If your profiles set `terminate-after`, leave room for queueing.
  - These are still not scheduled: test binaries run directly, doctests, `--no-run`, commands with `--config`, `+toolchain` or `-C`, and `--archive-file` runs built for a triple that is neither the requested target nor the host.

- **The `mbx doctor` archives check falls back to `llvm-ar` and `llvm-ranlib`** when `ar` or `ranlib` isn't on `PATH`, for example on Windows ([#699](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/699), @Veykril). Each tool falls back separately. If a tool runs but fails, mbx reports that error instead of trying the fallback. This changes only the host probe. It doesn't change which archiver build scripts use.

## Fixed

- **`mbx nextest run -j N` no longer limits the build to N compiler permits** ([#685](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/685), @jbellis). For nextest, `-j`, `--jobs` and `--test-threads` set how many tests run at once, so mbx now ignores them as build limits. It reads `--build-jobs N` instead, and still falls back to `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS`. This also works through Cargo aliases. Alias expansion no longer runs `cargo --list`, which saves one Cargo subprocess per external command.
- **Setting an explicit linker no longer makes rlib and `cargo check` compilations skip the cache** ([#694](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/694), @jdx). A target `linker = "clang"` (for example, with `-C link-arg=-fuse-ld=mold`) made every library and check compilation report `unknown-codegen-option`, even though they never link. These compilations are now cached, and the linker is still part of the cache key. Outputs that actually link keep their existing restrictions.
- **`-L native=` directories no longer cause misses across checkouts or target dirs** ([#692](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/692), @jdx). Build scripts such as `libz-sys` and `aws-lc-sys` leave files there that the linker never reads but that contain the absolute target path. mbx now skips `pkgconfig/`, `cmake/` and `*.dSYM/` directories, plus `.pc`, `.cmake` and C/C++ header files, when hashing these directories. Libraries are still hashed.
- **A `-L native=` directory passed more than once now counts once against the 2 GiB native input limit** ([#691](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/691), @jdx). A build script that printed the same `rustc-link-search` line twice could double a 1.2 GiB directory past the limit, so the result wasn't stored (`rustc search path kind is not cacheable yet: native`). A directory nested inside another `-L native=` directory is also counted once now.
- **Crates whose build script declares `rerun-if-env-changed=OUT_DIR` build again** ([#700](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/700), @jdx). This is what `build-rs` emits for `build_rs::input::out_dir()`. Crates that included generated sources from `OUT_DIR` failed with `compilation result was discarded: build-script inputs changed during compilation`. They now build and are cached, and two checkouts of the same project share the cache entry.
- **Workspace libraries with a `staticlib`, `cdylib` or `dylib` crate type now compile incrementally** ([#695](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/695), @jdx). mbx doesn't cache these libraries, such as Tauri's `["staticlib", "cdylib", "rlib"]` template, and until now it also rebuilt them from scratch on every edit. They now get learned incremental state on the first build and reuse it after that. They're still reported as `unsupported-crate-type` bypasses. `learned_incremental = false` (`MBX_LEARNED_INCREMENTAL=0`), `MBX_VERIFY`, or a user-set `-Cincremental` turns this off.
- **Running `mbx` through a symlink and through its real path now gives the same `HOST_CC`** ([#693](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/693), @jdx). Before, the two paths used different C/C++ shim directories. So switching between `mbx build` and plain `cargo` (through the cargo shim) in the same target dir reran every build script that watches `HOST_CC`. Upgrading in place at the same real path still keeps the same shim directory. If you reach versioned installs through a moving `latest` symlink, each release now gets its own shim directory, so cc-based build scripts rerun once after each upgrade.

## New Contributors

* @Veykril made their first contribution in [#699](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/699)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/compare/v1.23.0...v1.24.0
